items.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: In those days it was called Gene Autrey’s Continental Hotel

ctx.x: What was it like moving from New York to L.A.? Were you glad that happened at the time?

I like them both as long as it’s one or the other. But it was easy. They, when we used to come out to visit before we moved here, we’d come out for two or three weeks a couple of times a year. And this was before the Sheraton Universal Hotel was even built. So we used to have to stay way down in Hollywood at what is now the Hyatt on Sunset. In those days it was called Gene Autrey’s Continental Hotel, and we had to drive. Now that’s in the late 60s. About 70, the Sheraton Universal got built so we’d stay there, it…
What’s it like today doing, you’re still doing studio work and has that changed over the years with how studios have changed and electronics and all that. Has that affected your business?
